name: Two buttons on a goods lift
brief:
A warehouse goods lift serves floors 1 to `n`. It has two buttons: Up moves it exactly `u` floors and Down exactly `d` floors. A press that would take it below floor 1 or above floor `n` does nothing, so it is never worth making.

The input comes as one string holding five whole numbers, `n`, `s`, `g`, `u` and `d`, separated by spaces or newlines. The lift starts on floor `s` and must reach floor `g`.

Write `solve_lift_buttons(text)`, which returns, as a string, the fewest presses that take the lift from `s` to `g`, or `"-1"` if no presses can. Expect extra spaces and a trailing newline.

Example. For `"10 1 10 2 1\n"` the route 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 8, 10 takes 6 presses. Going up five times reaches 11, which is above the top floor, so the answer is `"6"`.
constraints: $1 \le s, g \le n \le 500{,}000$ and $0 \le u, d \le n$.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Trying every sequence of presses is far too slow.
Each test has its own 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Each floor is a node with at most two edges out. Search outward from `s` level by level, and mark a floor the first time you reach it.

examples.note: Five presses of Up would pass the top floor, so one Down press is needed on the way.
Up does nothing and Down only goes lower, so floor 4 cannot be reached.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: The floors form a graph with two edges out of each, so breadth-first search finds the fewest presses.
Without a mark on each visited floor the search revisits floors forever; with `u` or `d` equal to 0 a press goes nowhere and is skipped.
Each floor joins the queue at most once, so the work is $O(n)$ time and $O(n)$ memory.
